findings.reason: without a followup naming §51 the roadmap shows no invocation for it, so the section never runs; this is exactly the wiring defect §46 had, which a prior review raised and the plan acted on.
findings.text: §51 is declared implementable in both plan-section-declarations and its section element, but the followups block (ending at f-tmstwiw-050, which names §50) carries no f-tmstwiw-051, so nothing in the roadmap will dispatch it

findings.reason: the node's gate asserts both a dedup property and a protocol behaviour, so a reviewer cannot close the node on one verdict and a failing release path leaves the lift fix unreviewed.
findings.text: the Deliverable states "Every follower a session host runs shares one lift claim per pane…" and then "The session host also accepts a release request", two independent mechanisms in different modules (crew_follow_commands.py versus session_host.py) with independent acceptance conditions, under a title that names only the lift

findings.reason: a host-side handler with no client never fires, so the "follower handed over by mistake stays until the owning Claude process ends" problem the Why cites is not closed by adding it; the section must name the caller it relies on or drop the deliverable.
findings.text: the release request "naming a project and session" has no named caller: the only writer of the host's request FIFO is _request_host_follower, which sends a follow request {project, session} (reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:636-674), and the plan names no client, command or code path that would ever send a release line

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — lift_claim_dir (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1126, keyed on session as claimed), parse_request (reckon/crew/session_host.py:189, reads only project and session as claimed) and _session_host_owner (reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:500) all resolve; §23, §25, §49 and §50 exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §51 declares a negative control ("keys the claim on the session again, and the two-session case then draws two rows"), and each case names an observable in the host's output.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is logged "under the run directory", a durable path that survives the run, not a session scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section title and the test name test_a_pane_draws_a_lift_once_per_host.py state the mechanism; no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §51's release-request mechanism names no caller that would ever send a release line, so the capability it adds is reached by no production path.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §51's Deliverable carries two mechanisms that are not the same goal: rekeying the lift claim on the host owner, and a new release-request protocol in the session host.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §51 is declared implementable but no followup names it: the followups block ends at f-tmstwiw-050 (which names §50), so the roadmap surfaces no invocation that will ever dispatch §51.
